messages:
alice_support: Customer hit a 500 on text.generate, says "no trace id in UI" and app logs show only a short 'upstream error'. Need minimal repro + where they can find any trace/correlation tokens.

sam_engineer: Thanks — first ask for the exact timestamp + request payload. Also ask them to dump the response headers from the failing request (the API returns request headers when present).

morgan_mobile: For mobile SDKs customers often miss the SDK debug token. Ask them to call the SDK helper: `Redwood.getDebugToken()` (iOS/Android/Web vary, share snippet).

alice_support: Sharing a short checklist I usually send: 1) exact ISO timestamp 2) full request body (json) 3) response status + full response headers 4) client logs (10s before/after) 5) SDK debug token or server request-id.

sam_engineer: Sample curl they can run (replace <KEY> and <PAYLOAD>):
```bash
curl -v https://api.redwoodinference.example/v1/generate \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <KEY>' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"model":"redwood-alpha","input":"hello world"}' \
  --write-out '\nHTTP_CODE:%{http_code}\nREQUEST_ID:%{header_x_request_id}\n'
```
Note: --write-out reads `header_x_request_id` on many curl builds; if empty they can inspect the `-v` output for any `x-request-id` or `x-trace-token` headers.

morgan_mobile: Mobile-specific: in app dev consoles look for these places: Android OkHttp interceptors -> response.header("x-request-id") ; iOS URLSession -> task.response?.allHeaderFields["x-request-id"] ; Web -> Network tab -> the failing request -> Response Headers. If our SDK surfaced a debug token, that's `x-redwood-debug-token` in logs.

alice_support: If they can't run curl, ask for a HAR from the browser or a tcpdump/Charles trace for mobile. In the HAR the path is `entries[*].response.headers` — grab headers matching request-id / trace / debug-token.

sam_engineer: For server-side repro we'd love: server logs showing the outbound request (headers/body), the API response body and headers, and the local timestamp. If they have proxy/load-balancer, include that trace id too.

alice_support: If they send a debug bundle please include a short README line naming the key file that contains the `x-request-id` or `x-trace-token` so engs don't have to hunt. :pray:

deploy-bot: new-incident-created #INC-6152 - attaching CI alert window 2026-03-17T15:30:10Z

sam_engineer: If they share the `x-request-id` we can map it to our logs and return a short trace snippet. If they can't find any header, ask them to run the curl above and paste back the `REQUEST_ID:` line or the verbose headers.

morgan_mobile: Quick phrasing you can paste to customers:
"Can you please provide: 1) exact timestamp (UTC), 2) the request body, 3) the full response headers (or HAR), and 4) any SDK debug token (`Redwood.getDebugToken()` / `x-redwood-debug-token`)? With the `x-request-id`/`x-trace-token` we can locate the server-side trace immediately."

alice_support: Great — i'll send that now and ask them to run the curl if possible. Thanks. :thumbsup:
